background.t: In the last election, in July 2023, the PP won the most seats (137), ahead of the Socialists (121) and Vox (33). Sánchez stayed in power with the support of smaller parties.
Many Spaniards are angry about the cost of housing. Sánchez wanted the campaign to be about that.

ctx.intro: Pedro Sánchez has led Spain since 2018. In the 2023 election the conservative PP won the most seats, but Sánchez kept power with the support of smaller parties. In October 2026 parliament rejected his housing plans, and he called an early election.

tl.t: General election: the PP wins the most seats, but Sánchez stays in power with the support of smaller parties.
Parliament rejects the government’s emergency housing measures. Sánchez calls an election for 29 November.

effects.label: Who governs Spain
effects.t: If the polls are right, the PP would need Vox to reach a majority. That would be a first at national level.

effects.label: Housing
effects.t: Sánchez called the vote over housing. The result decides whose plan for rents and building goes ahead.

effects.label: Europe
effects.t: A PP–Vox majority would move another large EU country to the right.

event.t: The official campaign began on Friday 13 November and runs until 27 November. Voting is on Sunday 29 November.
Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called the early vote on 5 October, after parliament rejected his government’s emergency housing measures.
Most private polls put the conservative People’s Party (PP) first. They give PP and Vox together about 190 to 200 of the 350 seats; 176 are needed for a majority.

The state polling institute, the CIS, shows a different picture: Socialists first on 33.3%, PP on 25.5% and Vox on 18.4%, leaving PP and Vox short of a majority. It has differed from private polls before.
A high-speed train crash that killed 69 people on 28 October changed the campaign. Transport minister Óscar Puente resigned six days later.
The main issues are the cost of housing, immigration, corruption allegations and rail safety.

headline: Spain’s election campaign is under way, with the right ahead in most polls

items.text: He asks voters to defend his government’s social policies against a possible PP–Vox majority.
It promises an audit of public spending under the Socialists and campaigns on housing and on corruption allegations against the government.
It campaigns on immigration: priority for Spaniards in public aid, and an end to large-scale regularisations of migrants.

sh: Spain votes on 29 Nov: right leads most polls
simple: Spain is voting early, on 29 November, because the prime minister could not pass his housing plans. Most polls say the two parties on the right would together win enough seats to govern. One large public poll says the opposite, so the result is not certain.

summary: Spain votes in an early general election on Sunday 29 November. Most polls say the conservative People’s Party would win but need the Vox party to govern. The state pollster instead puts Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s Socialists first.

terms.v: An election called earlier than scheduled.
The number needed for a majority in Spain’s 350-seat lower house of parliament.
The People’s Party (PP) is Spain’s main conservative party. The PSOE, or Socialists, is the main centre-left party, led by Pedro Sánchez.
A nationalist party to the right of the PP. Reuters describes it as right-wing; France 24 and Anadolu call it far-right.
Spain’s state-run polling institute. Its results often differ from those of private pollsters.

why: Spain is the euro area’s fourth-largest economy. A change of government would shift its course on housing, immigration and public spending. If the polls are right, the conservatives would depend on Vox, which has never been part of a national government.

updates.t: Three polls published on Monday show that the PP and Vox would together win a majority, Reuters reports, while the Socialists gain ground. In the daily 40dB poll for El País, the Socialists pass 30% for the first time, on 30.3%, and the PP and Vox together have 192 seats.
updates.why: They are the first polls since the campaign began.
